That proximity to builders is valuable whether you're evaluating a new protocol, looking for collaboration opportunities, or just trying to understand what's actually happening on-chain.

For anyone building on Solana or considering it, these AMAs are a low-commitment way to stay connected. There's no ticket price, no travel required, and the community aspect means you're not just consuming content — you're plugging into a network of people who are actively building. That network effect is often where the real value of events like this shows up, weeks or months after the call ends.

The fact that this particular session had 17 attendees marked as 'went' speaks to the engaged nature of the Superteam India community. In a space where many events struggle to attract consistent audiences, a weekly series that maintains participation is a sign that the format is meeting a real need.

luma-host-evt-uZcNvXgLxoQ26if.summaryLead: A virtual poker night hosted by Superteam India on Nomad Poker, pitting community members against each other for a 500 Devnet SOL prize pool.

sections.heading: The Concept Behind Poker Night
content: Superteam India Poker Night flips the typical crypto meetup format on its head. Instead of panels and presentations, you get a poker table. The event runs on Nomad Poker, a platform built for exactly this kind of community competition, and the stakes are real — at least in devnet terms. The prize pool is 500 SOL on devnet, which makes it a fun way to test your poker instincts without putting actual funds on the line.

The event is organized by the same crew behind the AMA with Atharv series, including hosts Atharv Velhal, Fahad Khan, Kshitij Gajapure, and Paarug. It's clearly designed as a social event first, with the competition aspect adding energy rather than intimidation. Superteam India describes the vibe as poker, competition, and community — a combination that works surprisingly well when everyone shares a professional interest in the same ecosystem.

The free pizza mention in the event description is a playful touch that nods to in-person poker culture. Even though this is a virtual event, the organizers are keeping the spirit alive by creating the feeling of sitting around a table with friends rather than staring at a screen in isolation.

sections.heading: Playing on Nomad Poker
content: Nomad Poker is the platform that makes this work. It's designed for crypto communities to host poker games, and the Superteam India event uses it to run what amounts to a private tournament. You can try the platform ahead of time at nomadpoker.fun to get comfortable with the interface before the actual event, which is a smart move for anyone who hasn't played online poker before.

The virtual format means anyone in the Superteam India community can join regardless of where they're physically located. Registration happens through the Luma event page, and once you're in, you'll be competing against fellow community members who share your interest in Solana and the broader crypto space. The barrier to entry is low, which is part of the appeal.

Devnet SOL as the prize currency is an interesting choice. It keeps the competition fun and accessible while still giving winners something to talk about. Nobody's risking their rent money, but the bragging rights are real. And in a community where reputation and connections matter, those bragging rights can translate into genuine social capital.

sections.heading: Community Building Through Cards
content: Events like this serve a dual purpose. On the surface, it's a fun way to spend an evening competing for bragging rights and a devnet prize pool. Underneath, it's a networking opportunity that doesn't feel like one. When you're playing cards with someone, conversations happen naturally, and you end up learning about what other people are building without the forced structure of a networking session.

The 19 people who showed up to the event represent a cross-section of the Superteam India community — builders, enthusiasts, and people who are just curious about what's happening in the Solana space. For a recurring community event, that kind of organic participation is a strong signal that the format works. It's the kind of thing that makes people come back, not for the poker, but for the connections they make at the table.

There's something to be said for events that don't take themselves too seriously. The crypto space is full of high-stakes conferences and intense hackathons. A poker night where the biggest risk is losing bragging rights provides a counterbalance to all that intensity, and the community is clearly responding to it.

luma-host-evt-nlLYpU09DZISw4E.summaryLead: An early morning group workout in Belgrade's Tašmajdan park during Belgrade Blockchain Week 2026, hosted by Wirex, CTRL community, Mighty Study, and Tangem.

sections.heading: What Happens at COW
content: Crypto Outdoor Workout — COW for short — is exactly what it sounds like: a group fitness session held outdoors, organized around major crypto conferences. The Belgrade edition takes place at Street gym in Tašmajdan park, starting at 6:00 AM. It's designed to be accessible to any fitness level, which means you can show up whether you're a seasoned athlete or someone who just wants to stretch before a long day of conference sessions.

The workout itself covers the fundamentals: warmup, squats, pushups, chin-ups, dips, abs, and stretches. There's also a pljeskavice thrown in — a playful reference to Serbian food culture that hints at the local flavor of this particular edition. Coaches are on hand to guide you through the movements, but you're also free to work out at your own pace, join or leave whenever you want, and generally treat it as a flexible start to the day.

The event is tagged under both Crypto and Fitness on Luma, capturing the dual nature of what's happening. It's not just a workout with a crypto label, and it's not just a crypto networking event held in a gym. It's genuinely both, appealing to people who want to move their bodies and meet people outside the usual exhibition hall setting.

sections.heading: The Sponsors and Their Roles
content: This edition is supported by four organizations, each bringing something different to the table. Wirex is the headline sponsor — a global payments platform that has been around since 2014 and has served over 7 million users across 130 countries. They've processed more than $20 billion in transactions and are a principal Visa and Mastercard member, which positions them at the intersection of crypto and traditional payments. For a workout event at a blockchain conference, that sponsorship makes sense.

CTRL is a non-profit community of open-source contributors, adding a developer-focused angle to the sponsorship. Tangem, a Swiss hardware wallet provider, brings the self-custody perspective — they've sold over 6 million card-shaped wallets that let users hold and manage thousands of coins offline without cables, batteries, or Bluetooth. ETHBelgrade, the Ethereum event happening in Belgrade during the same week, rounds out the support. The combination spans payments, open source, hardware, and the broader Ethereum community.

The diversity of sponsors reflects the cross-chain, cross-sector nature of the COW community. This isn't a single-protocol event; it's a gathering that welcomes anyone in the crypto space who wants to start their morning with physical activity and good company.

sections.heading: The Track Record and What Makes It Stick
content: COW has been running at crypto conferences for two years now, and the Belgrade edition is described as a return to where it all started. Previous editions have happened at Berlin Blockchain Week, EthCC in Cannes, Consensus Hong Kong, Devconnect Buenos Aires, Token2049 Singapore, and a dozen other events across Europe, Asia, and South America. That track record suggests the format fills a real need — conference attendees want a way to move their bodies and meet people outside the usual exhibition hall setting.

This particular session also comes with extras: drinking water, high-protein snacks, and limited edition merch. The organizers are clearly investing in making the experience worth showing up for, even at 6:00 AM. With 76 people registered for the Belgrade edition, it's one of the larger COW events, which makes sense given that Belgrade has become a significant hub for blockchain events in the Balkans.

The longevity of the COW series matters. When an event keeps showing up at conference after conference, it builds its own community of regulars. People plan their conference schedules around it, knowing they'll get a workout, some fresh air, and conversations with people they actually want to talk to. That kind of recurring, trusted event is rare in the crypto space, where everything tends to be new and untested.

luma-host-evt-c6CVoUpEc63KnuY.summaryLead: A weekly Wednesday evening gathering in Bangkok where founders, developers, and builders combine recovery sessions with genuine networking at ARAH ice bath and sauna facility.

sections.heading: The Wednesday Recovery Ritual
content: Founder Wellness & Networking Series is a weekly event organized by Superteam Thailand that runs every Wednesday evening in Bangkok. The concept is simple: founders and builders in tech, AI, and Web3 need a way to recharge midweek, and the organizers figured that combining wellness activities with networking would be more effective than another panel discussion. The result is an evening that starts with food and drinks and moves into a structured recovery circuit.

The timeline is straightforward. From 5:30 to 6:30 PM, attendees settle in with healthy food and drinks, reconnect with familiar faces, and make new introductions in a casual setting. From 6:30 to 8:30 PM, the focus shifts to the recovery circuit at ARAH, which includes sauna, ice bath, cold plunge, swimming pool access, and a candlelit recovery space. The entire experience costs 500 THB, which covers the recovery facilities.

The progression from social hour to recovery session is deliberate. By the time people hit the ice bath, they've already had real conversations with the people around them. That shared experience of cold water and heat therapy creates a bond that a cocktail hour alone can't replicate. It's wellness with a social purpose.

sections.heading: Breaking from the Usual Meetup Format
content: Superteam Thailand positions this explicitly against the traditional meetup format. No presentations, no panels, no endless pitching. Instead, the emphasis is on genuine conversations with some of Bangkok's most ambitious builders. The organizer behind it is OnlyFounders, working in partnership with Superteam Thailand to create something that feels more like a regular gathering of peers than a one-off event.

The audience includes founders, developers, designers, creators, investors, and operators. Whether you're actively building a startup or simply looking to meet ambitious people in Bangkok, you're welcome. The event is tagged under Tech and Wellness on Luma, and it's been featured in the Bangkok discovery section, which means it's getting visibility beyond just the Superteam Thailand community.

The sold-out status — 68 people registered — speaks to the demand for this kind of event in Bangkok. The city has become a major hub for Web3 builders and digital nomads, but the social scene often revolves around bars and loud venues. This provides an alternative that's both healthier and more conducive to actual conversation.

sections.heading: The Venue and Why It Works
content: ARAH is located at 88, 8 Sukhumvit 49 in the Khlong Tan Nuea area of Watthana, Bangkok. It's a dedicated facility for ice baths, saunas, and hot tubs — not a hotel wellness center or a repurposed gym. The specific address puts it in one of Bangkok's more accessible neighborhoods for the expat and tech community that tends to overlap with the Web3 scene.

For founders who spend their days staring at screens, managing teams, and making decisions under pressure, the recovery aspect isn't a gimmick. Cold plunges and sauna sessions have genuine benefits for stress reduction and mental clarity, and combining that with networking means you're investing in both your physical health and your professional network at the same time.

The weekly cadence is what makes this particularly valuable. One-off wellness events at conferences are nice, but they don't build habits. By running every Wednesday, Superteam Thailand is creating a ritual that founders can build their weeks around. The regularity means the community deepens over time, with people forming real relationships rather than collecting business cards at a single event.

luma-evt-6AOHAASiPKsinbz.summaryLead: The annual general assembly of DAO Suisse, covering governance review, elections, and strategic outlook at Dezentrum in Zürich.

sections.heading: The Formal Business at Hand
content: DAO Suisse General Assembly 2026 is the official annual meeting of DAO Suisse, a Swiss association operating in the crypto space. The event takes place on August 26 at Dezentrum in Zürich, running from 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM. It follows the standard structure of a Swiss association general assembly, with a clear agenda that covers the essentials: a recap of the organization's second year, the discharge and realignment process, elections, and the financial statement.

The formal portion runs from 5:00 PM to 6:15 PM, broken into five segments of 15 minutes each. After arrival and the recap of the second year, the assembly moves through discharge and realignment, elections and the financial statement, and concludes with an outlook on future initiatives. This is where the organization's governance gets exercised — motions, votes, and the kind of democratic process that gives associations their legitimacy.

Motions from association members had to be submitted at least 15 days before the assembly, which is standard governance practice for Swiss associations. This requirement ensures that proposals are reviewed and discussed before the actual meeting, keeping the assembly focused on decision-making rather than lengthy deliberation on new items.

sections.heading: Virtual and In-Person Participation
content: One practical detail that stands out: the assembly offers a virtual attendance option via Microsoft Teams. For an organization operating in the crypto space, this hybrid approach makes sense — not every member can travel to Zürich, but everyone should have the chance to participate in governance decisions. The Teams link is provided on the event page, making it straightforward to join remotely.

In-person attendees get the added benefit of the apéro that follows the formal business, starting at 6:15 PM. This is where the real community building happens — after the votes are cast and the financials are reviewed, members can connect over drinks and discuss what the assembly revealed about the organization's direction. The informal conversations at events like this often matter as much as the formal proceedings.

The venue, Dezentrum at Lessingstrasse 15 in the 8002 postal code of Zürich, is a known gathering spot in the city's crypto and tech community. Choosing a familiar venue reduces friction for attendees and signals that this is a community event, not a corporate function held in a sterile conference room.

sections.heading: Why This Assembly Matters
content: For members of DAO Suisse, this is the annual checkpoint where the organization's past year gets reviewed and its future gets shaped. The discharge process is where members approve or question how the board has managed the association, and the elections determine who will lead it going forward. The financial statement provides transparency into how resources have been allocated and whether the organization is on solid financial footing.

The timing is also notable. Coming in late August, the assembly sets the tone for the fall and winter programming. The outlook and future initiatives segment is where new directions get proposed, which makes it relevant not just for current members but for anyone considering getting involved with DAO Suisse. It's a window into what the organization plans to prioritize in the months ahead.

With 11 people registered to attend, it's a small but engaged group — the kind of setting where individual voices actually matter in governance decisions. In larger organizations, your vote gets diluted among thousands. At an assembly like this, each person's input carries weight. For anyone interested in how crypto-native organizations handle governance in practice, watching DAO Suisse operate is instructive.

luma-evt-XJRrcu8kmK4u3aN.summaryLead: A women-only event in Zürich exploring the intersection of relationships, personal finance, and Bitcoin, presented by SatoShe with therapist Ramona Zenger.

sections.heading: The Psychology Behind Money Conflicts
content: Liebe, Geld & Bitcoin — Love, Money & Bitcoin — tackles something most people avoid talking about: how couples handle finances. The event is structured around a simple premise that money is one of the most common sources of conflict in relationships and simultaneously one of the biggest taboos. SatoShe, a Bitcoin education organization focused on women, brings together two perspectives that complement each other: couples therapy and Bitcoin education.

The evening features Ramona Zenger, a couples and psychotherapist who has appeared on the Blick podcast 'intim&laut' and SRF's 'Deep Dating.' She'll explain why money conversations so often end in conflict and what's psychologically behind those patterns. Beyond the psychology, the event covers the financial reality of women in Switzerland — wage gaps, part-time work, care work, pension funds, and prenuptial agreements, all presented in an accessible way that doesn't require a finance background.

The combination of therapeutic expertise and financial education is unusual. Most crypto events focus purely on the technical or investment side of things. By starting with the psychological dynamics of money conversations, this event acknowledges that financial decisions don't happen in a vacuum — they happen within relationships, and those relationships have their own complexities.

sections.heading: Bitcoin as a Foundation for Long-Term Wealth
content: The Bitcoin portion of the evening is designed for people with no prior knowledge. It starts with a brief, accessible introduction to why the current monetary system pushes people to work and invest more, and how hard money changes that dynamic. From there, it moves into practical applications: building wealth for children, managing inheritance, and navigating the trust question around private keys in a partnership.

The event also addresses the social dynamics of introducing Bitcoin to a resistant or misinformed partner. This is a common friction point in relationships where one person is interested in crypto and the other isn't, and the session provides concrete strategies for handling those conversations without damaging the relationship. A scientifically grounded couple's exercise is included as a takeaway, designed to strengthen financial conversations at home.

By framing Bitcoin not as a speculative investment but as a tool for long-term financial planning, the event positions it as something that benefits the whole family. The inheritance and children angle is particularly compelling — it moves the conversation beyond portfolio allocation and into legacy building, which resonates differently than typical crypto pitch decks.

sections.heading: Practical Details and Who Should Attend
content: The event takes place at MME Legal | Tax | Compliance on Zollstrasse 62 in Zürich, a venue that signals legal and financial credibility. Doors open at 6:00 PM with the program starting at 6:15 PM, running until approximately 9:00 PM. Tickets are CHF 49, with a discounted rate of CHF 39 for SatoShe Circle members. An apéro is included in the ticket price.

The evening is explicitly labeled as ladies only, though it's open to all women regardless of relationship status. The format is interactive, starting with an open round and encouraging questions and experiences from attendees. SatoShe Circle members get additional benefits, including session credits for annual members. The event carries a disclaimer that it's for educational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice.

For women in Zürich who are curious about Bitcoin and want to understand how it fits into personal financial planning within a relationship, this is a rare combination of relationship advice and crypto education. The 17 people registered so far represent a mix of SatoShe Circle members and newcomers, which suggests the event is reaching both its core audience and people who are just getting started.

luma-evt-uxBdBwfsP6xBJEX.summaryLead: Toronto Open Data heads to Etobicoke Civic Centre on August 26 for a hands-on jam session where residents can dig into city data and shape local council motions — samosas included.

sections.heading: What This Jam Session Is Really About
content: The City of Toronto's Open Data team runs monthly meetups across the city, and for August they're setting up in the Etobicoke Council Chamber at 399 The West Mall. The idea is straightforward: show people how open data works at the municipal level, then let them apply it to actual Etobicoke City Council motions. It's civic tech at its most local and practical.

The session kicks off with a program intro covering the City of Toronto's open data platform at open.toronto.ca, how the program operates, and practical ways attendees can use the data in their own projects or advocacy work. Then the team spotlights specific Etobicoke council motions and the datasets that inform them. No abstract theory here — you're looking at real policy discussions backed by real numbers pulled directly from the city's open data portal.

After the presentations, the event shifts into an open brainstorm where residents connect with each other and talk through how open data could improve life in Etobicoke. That might mean mapping transit gaps, analyzing housing stats, tracking where city spending goes, or identifying patterns in community services that aren't obvious from the outside. The Open Data team also wants direct feedback on what datasets would be most useful to release or improve, which is a rare opportunity to shape the pipeline of public information.

sections.heading: The People in the Room and What They Bring
content: You'll find technologists, public servants, and civic enthusiasts all in the same room. The networking isn't an afterthought — it's baked into the format. This is where people find collaborators for data projects, learn about job opportunities in municipal government, or just swap ideas over food. The Etobicoke edition brings together residents who might not normally make it to the downtown meetups, which means the perspectives in the room skew toward local, neighborhood-level concerns.

Toronto Open Data is presented by the City of Toronto's Technology Services Division, and the events are hosted by Ilya Kreynin. The team has built a consistent monthly rhythm that keeps the community engaged without overwhelming anyone's calendar. Forty-one people were already registered for this session, suggesting a healthy mix of returning attendees and newcomers curious about what open data can do for their corner of the city.

sections.heading: Practical Details and How to Prepare
content: The event runs from 6:00 PM to 8:30 PM Eastern on Tuesday, August 26, inside the Etobicoke Council Chamber. The venue is at 399 The West Mall, Etobicoke, ON M9C 2Y2, and is accessible by TTC. Being in the actual council chamber adds a certain weight to the proceedings — you're sitting where decisions get made, talking about the data that shapes those decisions.

Registration is free through Luma, and the City collects basic personal information under the authority of the City of Toronto Act, 2006, for the purposes of improving the Open Data Program and identifying datasets that could be released. If you're interested in how your city uses data, or if you want to learn how municipal open data actually works in practice, this is a low-barrier way to get involved. The samosas are a nice bonus.

luma-host-evt-T2tQkKnZEqXWxYO.summaryLead: Superteam India's weekly community call brings together Solana builders every Thursday at 6 PM IST for demos, wins, and ecosystem updates — a recurring touchpoint for one of crypto's most active regional communities.

sections.heading: How Superteam India Actually Works
content: Superteam operates as a gated Slack workspace for operators, developers, and grantees building on Solana. There's no treasury, no commissions, no token sale. Revenue goes to the individual members or teams who win bounties, secure grants, or raise funding for their ideas. The framing is intentional: a collective of sovereigns rather than a sovereign collective. This distinction matters because it shapes how people interact within the community — as independent operators who choose to collaborate, not as employees following a central plan.

Membership is based on criteria that filter for people actively contributing to the Solana ecosystem. Once you're in, you get access to the community itself, which Superteam considers the actual product. The India chapter, hosted by Paarug and the Superteam India team, has grown to 232 registered attendees for this particular call, suggesting real momentum in the region. The gated nature of the community means conversations stay focused on building rather than marketing or speculation.

Superteam's broader network spans multiple countries and regions, but the India chapter has developed its own distinct identity. The hosts — Paarug and the Superteam India team — maintain active presences on Instagram and X, sharing updates between calls and keeping the community engaged throughout the week. The social layer matters because it transforms a weekly call into an ongoing relationship.

sections.heading: What Happens on the Weekly Call
content: Every Thursday at 6:00 PM IST, the community gathers on Zoom. The call follows a loose but consistent format: celebrate member wins, share project updates and demos, help people find teammates, hear from occasional guest speakers, and get ecosystem news. It's structured enough to be useful but casual enough that you can drop in and out without feeling like you've missed something critical.

For someone building on Solana in India, this is a weekly checkpoint that keeps you connected to what's happening across the ecosystem. You can prototype a feature and demo it to the group, find a co-founder who complements your skills, or just hear what other teams are working on. The approval-required registration means this isn't a marketing event open to anyone with an email address — it's a working session for people actually building things.

The guest speaker element adds variety without dominating the format. Some weeks feature founders or developers from prominent Solana projects; other weeks are purely internal. The demo component is particularly valuable because it creates accountability — when you commit to showing something next Thursday, you actually build it. That cadence drives real progress across the community.

sections.heading: Why the Timing Matters for Solana in India
content: India's Web3 developer community has grown rapidly over the past few years, and Solana has been a primary chain for Indian builders due to its low transaction costs and high throughput. Superteam's global model of regional chapters means India gets its own dedicated programming rather than being an afterthought in a US-centric schedule. The Thursday evening IST timing works well for builders who have day jobs or are working across time zones.

The 2026 community call series signals that Superteam is investing in this region for the long haul. India's developer talent pool is deep, but the ecosystem needs structured communities to channel that talent into productive work. Superteam fills that gap by providing not just a Slack channel but a regular gathering rhythm that builds trust and familiarity among builders who might otherwise never connect.

For anyone considering building on Solana from India, joining this call is about the lowest-friction way to plug into the network. You get exposure to active projects, real hiring needs, and a community that's already past the hype cycle and into the work of actually shipping products. The registration link is on Luma, and approval is based on your actual involvement in the ecosystem.

luma-host-evt-S1a3G141Dsg60pk.summaryLead: The Solana Ecosystem Call returns for its August edition — a monthly live show with late-night TV production values, hosted by SOL BROTHERS, drawing over 2,500 registered attendees.

sections.heading: A Crypto Show That Doesn't Feel Like a Crypto Show
content: The Solana Ecosystem Call is pitched as the boldest show in crypto, and the format backs that up. Each monthly episode uses sketches, in-depth interviews, data-driven segments, and unfiltered commentary to break down what matters across the Solana network. It's produced by SOL BROTHERS Studio, which also runs podcasts and host interviews. The production approach borrows from late-night television structure rather than the usual Web3 Twitter space format.

The show is explicitly designed to be cringe-intolerant — a direct contrast to the typical crypto space where someone talks at a static avatar for two hours. SOL BROTHERS bring actual production quality: edited segments, multiple hosts with real chemistry, and a commitment to making the content watchable beyond the core audience. Each episode covers sketches that break down complex topics, interviews with people doing the actual work, and unfiltered takes on what's working and what isn't.

SOL BROTHERS have built their studio around producing content that serves the Solana ecosystem specifically. Their YouTube and X channels host the full archive of past episodes, along with additional podcast content and host interviews. The studio's focus on Solana means they understand the ecosystem deeply enough to ask the right questions and push back when answers feel vague.

sections.heading: How the Community Feeds Into the Show
content: The Ecosystem Call isn't a one-way broadcast. Teams and projects can submit announcements, product launches, event promotions, and giveaway proposals through a public submission form on Linktree. The producers then curate what makes it onto the show, which means the content reflects what the community actually cares about rather than what a marketing team wants to push.

With 2,555 people registered for the August call, the show has become a genuine community gathering point. The hosts include the Solana Foundation, Eno, and Simon Molitor, giving it institutional backing while keeping the personalities front and center. The registration numbers suggest this is one of the larger regular virtual events in the Solana ecosystem, and the curated submission process keeps the quality bar consistent across episodes.

Solana itself is described as a high performance network powering internet capital markets, payments, AI agents, and crypto applications. The ecosystem call translates that technical breadth into digestible segments, helping people understand how different parts of the network connect and where the most interesting activity is happening.

sections.heading: Where to Watch and How to Get Involved
content: The August call is virtual, starting at 10:00 AM Pacific on Wednesday, August 27. Registration is free through Luma, and you can also watch directly on the ecosystemcall.com website. SOL BROTHERS maintains active YouTube and X channels for replays and announcements, so if you miss the live show, you can catch the recording within a reasonable window.

If you're building something on Solana and want exposure to a large, engaged audience, submitting to the show is worth the effort. The audience skews toward people who are already deep in the ecosystem, so you're reaching actual users and potential collaborators rather than passive spectators. The submission process is straightforward, and the producers are selective — getting featured carries more weight than a random tweet thread.

The show was featured in Superteam's programming, which adds another layer of community endorsement. For teams launching new products or protocols on Solana, timing a submission to coincide with the monthly Ecosystem Call can generate meaningful visibility. It's not a silver bullet, but it puts your work in front of thousands of people who are already paying attention to what's moving in the ecosystem.

luma-host-evt-YkyMEJ3vRCg9s29.summaryLead: Lido Labs Foundation leadership hosts the August tokenholder update on YouTube — a leadership keynote followed by audience Q&A covering protocol developments and what's next for the largest liquid staking protocol.

sections.heading: What the Poolside Update Covers
content: Lido's Poolside calls are the project's regular touchpoint with tokenholders and the broader community. The August session features a leadership keynote followed by an audience Q&A, which has been the consistent format across previous updates. The agenda is deliberately lean — one keynote, one Q&A — so the content stays focused on substance rather than padding. Previous recaps are available on the Lido blog for anyone who wants context on what's been discussed in earlier sessions.

The speakers for this session include Vasiliy, Executive Director at Lido Labs; Kate, Chief Operating Officer; Izzy, Chief of Staking at Lido Ecosystem; and Nemo, Team Lead at Wisp. This is senior leadership across operations and staking, which means the updates will cover both business direction and technical protocol work. Having the Chief of Staking on the call is particularly relevant because staking performance and validator operations are core to what Lido actually does.

The Wisp team lead's inclusion signals that new tooling or infrastructure around Lido's staking products may be part of the update. Wisp is a tooling project within the Lido ecosystem, and having Nemo on the call suggests there are concrete developments to share rather than just high-level strategy talk.

sections.heading: How to Watch and Submit Questions
content: The update streams on YouTube, Lido's X (Twitter), and LinkedIn simultaneously, starting at 7:00 AM Pacific on Wednesday, August 27. You register through Luma to add it to your calendar, but the actual viewing happens on the streaming platforms. The multi-platform streaming approach means you can watch wherever you're most comfortable, whether that's YouTube with live chat or X with real-time commentary from the community.

If you have a specific question for Lido's leadership, there's an anonymous submission form through Notion. This is a smart move — it removes the social pressure of asking a public question and lets people raise topics that might be uncomfortable to ask about openly. The team has committed to addressing submitted questions during the Q&A portion, which gives tokenholders a direct line to the people making decisions about the protocol's future.

Lido's social presence spans X, YouTube, and LinkedIn, and the Poolside format leverages all three. The YouTube channel hosts the full archive of past updates, making it easy to compare what leadership said three months ago with what they're saying now. That kind of accountability is uncommon in crypto, where project updates tend to be one-directional.

sections.heading: Why This Matters for Liquid Staking
content: Lido remains the dominant liquid staking protocol on Ethereum, and decisions made by its leadership ripple across the broader DeFi ecosystem. The Poolside format gives tokenholders direct access to the people making those decisions, which is rare in crypto governance. Most projects rely on governance forums and Snapshot votes; Lido adds a live, face-to-face component that builds trust and transparency.

For anyone holding stETH or LDO, or for teams building on top of Lido's liquid staking derivatives, these updates provide early signals about protocol changes, new integrations, and strategic direction. The August call comes at a time when the liquid staking landscape is getting more competitive, with new entrants and shifting validator dynamics. The Q&A portion is particularly valuable for understanding how Lido plans to maintain its position while addressing community concerns.

The Poolside series has built a consistent cadence that tokenholders can plan around. If you're a governance participant, these calls give you the context you need to vote informed rather than guessing. If you're a developer building on Lido's infrastructure, the leadership updates help you anticipate changes that might affect your integration. Either way, showing up matters.

luma-evt-C0Mv9v6TO711QCV.summaryLead: Paris's Ground Control venue hosts the August edition of Apéro Tricotant — a social knitting meetup where 35 people gather to craft, drink, and connect in the 12th arrondissement.

sections.heading: What Apéro Tricotant Actually Is
content: Apéro Tricotant is a French concept that combines apéro — the pre-dinner drinks and snacks tradition — with tricot, which means knitting. It's a social gathering where people bring their knitting projects, grab a drink, and work on their craft while chatting. Hosted by Mathilde through her Tricotant brand, the August 27 edition takes place at Ground Control, a popular cultural venue at 81 Rue du Charolais in Paris's 12th arrondissement.

This isn't a knitting class or a workshop with instructors. It's a casual meetup for people who already knit or crochet and want to do it in company. The vibe is social first, craft second. You show up, find a spot, and settle in for a few hours of making things alongside other people who share the same hobby. The concept taps into a growing appetite for analog, screen-free social activities that don't revolve around drinking culture alone.

The Tricotant brand has built a following in Paris through regular events that bring together people who might not otherwise meet. The Instagram presence at @tricotant showcases the community aesthetic — warm, colorful, and unpretentious. Mathilde has created something that feels distinctly Parisian in its casual elegance while remaining welcoming to newcomers.

sections.heading: The Venue and the Atmosphere
content: Ground Control is a multi-purpose cultural space in Paris known for hosting markets, concerts, food events, and community gatherings. It's a natural fit for a social crafting event — spacious, central, and set up for people to linger without feeling rushed. The August 27 edition runs from 5:30 PM to 9:30 PM, covering the prime apéro window and giving people plenty of time to settle in after work.

As of the listing, 35 people were registered and the event was full with a waitlist active. That tells you two things: the Tricotant community in Paris is healthy and growing, and Ground Control can accommodate a decent-sized gathering without losing the intimate feel. Mathilde hosts these regularly, and the consistent sellouts suggest the format resonates with people looking for community-oriented evening activities.

The 12th arrondissement location puts the event in a well-connected part of Paris, accessible by multiple metro lines. Ground Control sits in an area that's become known for its cultural programming, which means attendees can pair the meetup with dinner or drinks at the venue's own food offerings. The overlap between the crafting community and Ground Control's regular visitors creates a natural, relaxed atmosphere.

sections.heading: How to Get In and What to Expect
content: The event is currently at capacity, but Luma's waitlist system means you can still sign up and get notified if spots open up. People's plans change, especially for evening events that fall on a Wednesday, so waitlisted spots do come through more often than you might expect. If you're in Paris on August 27 and the idea of knitting with strangers in a cultural venue appeals to you, it's worth putting your name down.

The event is tagged under Arts & Culture on Luma, which fits — it's as much about the social and cultural experience as it is about the craft itself. No registration fee is listed, which is common for community socials of this type, though you'll want to bring your own supplies and budget for drinks at Ground Control. The format is low-commitment enough that you can show up for an hour or stay the full four hours depending on your schedule.

If you're visiting Paris and looking for a way to meet locals outside the typical tourist circuits, this is the kind of event that makes that possible. The shared activity of knitting gives people an immediate common ground, and the apéro format means the conversation flows naturally. You don't need to speak fluent French to participate — the craft itself transcends language barriers.

luma-evt-iKH2QHkjM7p0dPT.summaryLead: Part Two of R³ Group Bodywork's 'A New Way Forward' series lands at Pluto Toronto on August 27 — a two-hour guided session focusing on the core, diaphragm, ribs, and mid-back through bodywork, movement, and reflection.

sections.heading: What R³ Group Bodywork Is
content: R³ is a guided, body-led process developed by Lisa Nogueira that combines physical bodywork, movement, awareness, education, and reflection. It's not massage, yoga, or physical therapy — it sits in a space between somatic education and group therapy. Participants work on their own bodies at their own pace, with optional hands-on support from Lisa based on consent. The process is designed to be accessible to anyone regardless of their background in bodywork or movement.

The emphasis is on awareness rather than correction. The intention isn't to force the body to change or to fix something broken. Instead, R³ helps people notice what their body is already doing — the holding patterns, the bracing, the unconscious tension — and develop practical ways to respond differently when those familiar patterns show up. This approach recognizes that the body often responds before we consciously realize it, through a held breath, a tight stomach, or a back that keeps working to hold everything together.

sections.heading: What Part Two Specifically Addresses
content: This session focuses on the core, diaphragm, ribs, and mid-back — areas involved in breathing, support, and movement. The thematic lens for Part Two is pressure, effort, responsibility, and creating more room. It's designed for people who know what needs to change in their lives but find themselves tightening, bracing, or working harder when more is asked of them. The body responds to increased demands in predictable ways, and this session maps those physical responses to the themes they represent.

The session explores pressure and responsibility, effort and control, bracing and holding, and carrying more than is necessary. These aren't abstract concepts — they're mapped to specific physical areas that store and express those patterns. The three-part series builds from the ground up: Part One covered feet, legs, hips, and pelvis; Part Two moves to the midsection; Part Three will address shoulders, chest, neck, jaw, and head. Each part can be attended independently.

sections.heading: The Series Structure and Who It's For
content: A New Way Forward is a three-part series that takes a deliberate journey through the body. Part One, which happened on August 18, focused on support, weight, direction, and taking the next step through the lower body. Part Two, on August 27, turns to the core and breathing apparatus. Part Three, scheduled for September 3, completes the arc with expression, visibility, connection, and becoming more of yourself through the upper body and head.

You don't need previous bodywork, movement, or somatic experience to participate in any of the sessions. The format is designed to meet you where you are. Most of the work is done on your own body, and you can pause, modify, observe, or opt out of any part at any time. You'll remain fully clothed throughout, and optional hands-on support from Lisa is always based on your consent. This is a low-pressure environment for people who are curious about what their body is doing and why.

sections.heading: Practical Details and How to Register
content: Part Two takes place Thursday, August 27, from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM at Pluto Toronto, a community and coworking space at 60 Sumach Street, ground level. As of the listing, 16 people were registered and only 2 spots remained — this series is popular and filling fast. Tickets are available through Luma, with a Standard Pluto Member option that requires approval.

Wear comfortable clothing you can move in and bring a pillow for additional support. The venue at Pluto is a community-oriented space that aligns well with the group nature of the R³ process. Lisa Nogueira and Pluto Toronto co-host the event, and the R³ Group Bodywork Instagram at @r3bodywork has photos and context from previous sessions if you want to get a sense of the atmosphere before committing. Even if Part One has passed, jumping in at Part Two is explicitly welcomed.

mu-315990029.summaryLead: The ZK Learning Group kicks off a deep dive into ZkSync on August 27, 2026, bringing together developers and cryptography enthusiasts for a hands-on, zero-cost online session exploring zero knowledge proof applications.

sections.heading: What Is the ZK Learning Group?
content: The ZK Learning Group is a community-run initiative organized by the LFDT Seattle chapter of the Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust. It operates as a structured, year-long exploration of zero knowledge and SNARK programming in application development. Rather than a one-off talk or workshop, this group is designed as a recurring learning track where participants work through material systematically, covering different facets of ZK cryptography over time.

The coordination happens through the Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust Discord server, giving participants a dedicated space to ask questions, share resources, and stay connected between sessions. There is also a public GitHub repository at github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/zk-learning-group where lab materials and code are maintained, so attendees can follow along with practical exercises at their own pace.

sections.heading: This Session: Introduction to ZkSync
content: On August 27, the group focuses on ZkSync, one of the leading Layer 2 scaling solutions built on zero knowledge rollups. ZkSync uses cryptographic proofs to batch transactions off-chain and then verify them on Ethereum, reducing gas fees and increasing throughput without sacrificing security. This introductory session will walk through the core concepts behind ZkSync and how developers can start building on the platform.

The session is designed for anyone interested in ZK cryptography, from those just getting started with blockchain development to experienced engineers exploring new tooling. The Zoom meeting link is provided to registered attendees, and the organizers have noted that this event is shared across their global community. If you cannot attend live, signing up still gets you a link to the recording afterward, which makes this accessible regardless of your time zone.

sections.heading: Who Should Attend and What to Expect
content: This event is well suited for developers working in cryptography, blockchain security, and decentralized systems. If you have been curious about zero knowledge proofs but have not yet found a structured entry point, this learning group provides exactly that. The recurring nature of the sessions means you are not expected to absorb everything in a single sitting. Instead, you can build understanding incrementally alongside a community of peers.

At the time of writing, 61 attendees from 149 different groups had already marked themselves as going, which speaks to the broad interest in ZK education across the Meetup ecosystem. The session is labeled as a network event, meaning it is promoted beyond just the LFDT Seattle chapter. For anyone building or evaluating ZK-based applications, this is a solid opportunity to learn from practitioners who are actively working with the technology.

sections.heading: Practical Details
content: The session runs on August 27, 2026, starting at 9:00 AM Pacific Time. It is held entirely online, so there is no travel required. Registration is free through Meetup, and the Zoom link becomes visible to registered attendees before the event starts.

Make sure to join the Discord channel in advance if you want to participate in discussions outside of the live session. The GitHub repository is also worth bookmarking, as it contains the lab materials you will reference during the session. Having both set up beforehand will let you focus on the content rather than scrambling to create accounts or clone repos during the event.

mu-316021768.summaryLead: Francene hosts a recurring live demo of an AI-enhanced automated crypto trading platform on August 27, 2026, featuring a Q&A with the platform's founder and programmer for anyone curious about rules-based trading approaches.

sections.heading: What the Session Covers
content: This is a live online demonstration of a fully automated trading platform that uses AI and algorithmic strategies to trade across both stock and cryptocurrency markets. According to the host, the platform has been in development and operation for over 25 years, which is a remarkably long track record in the automated trading space. The session is designed to show participants exactly how the system identifies opportunities and manages risk in real time.

During the demo, you will see the platform operating live, which means watching actual trade decisions unfold rather than looking at slides or historical backtests. The founder and programmer will walk through how the AI components and trading algorithms work together, explain why market volatility can create opportunities for systematic traders, and share current market insights. There is also a dedicated Q&A segment where attendees can ask anything they want.

sections.heading: Beginner Friendly and Educational
content: The event is explicitly labeled as beginner friendly, covering blockchain networks, cryptocurrency, and AI. Whether you are brand new to crypto investing or already have a portfolio, the session is structured to meet you where you are. The host, Francene, describes herself as a Super Organizer on Meetup and notes that she has been running these live sessions with the founder for over a year. That repetition means the format is well polished and the presenters are accustomed to addressing a range of experience levels.

The core message is about removing emotion from trading through disciplined, rules-based automation. For anyone who has ever made a panic sell or a FOMO buy, this framing is appealing. The session does not push any particular investment strategy or product. Instead, it positions itself as educational, giving you the information to decide whether automated trading aligns with your goals.

sections.heading: How to Join and What to Know
content: Registration is required and must be completed through impactearnings.com/webinar to receive your live session link. This is not a casual drop-in event. You need to reserve your spot in advance to get the Zoom credentials. The session runs on August 27, 2026, at 11:00 AM Pacific Time and is held entirely online.

It is worth noting that this is a recurring event, happening every two weeks on Thursday through January 15, 2027. So if this particular date does not work for you, there are plenty of future opportunities to attend. The consistent schedule also suggests a committed community of returning participants, which can make the Q&A portions more productive as people build on previous discussions.

sections.heading: Things to Keep in Mind
content: As with any trading-related event, approach with a critical mind. Automated trading platforms carry risks, and past performance does not guarantee future results. The session is educational in nature, and the host frames it as an opportunity to learn and ask questions rather than a sales pitch. Still, do your own research before committing any capital to any trading system or platform.

The live format is genuinely useful for evaluation. Watching a system operate in real time is very different from reading a brochure or watching a recorded testimonial. You can observe how the platform handles market conditions as they actually happen, which gives you a much better sense of its behavior than any static presentation could provide.

content: KUB Global is positioning itself as a comprehensive, full-day event that brings together builders, partners, developers, institutions, payment leaders, investors, and the KUB Chain community under one roof. sections.heading: Why This Matters for Bangkok and Beyond
content: Bangkok has quietly become a significant hub for Web3 activity in Southeast Asia, and events like KUB Global reinforce that trajectory. The choice of ZillaSpace as the venue signals a certain level of production value and ambition. The venue is described as setting a new standard for event spaces, with modern design and central location.

For developers and builders working on payment infrastructure, tokenization, or DeFi in the Thai and broader Southeast Asian market, this event offers direct access to ecosystem partners who are actively investing in the region. luma-host-evt-n41e2dttG68htB5.summaryLead: Superteam India hosts a virtual workshop on August 28, 2026, for its gated community of Solana-focused operators, developers, and grantees looking to learn, earn, and build on the network.

sections.heading: What Superteam Actually Is
content: Superteam is frequently misunderstood, so it is worth explaining clearly. It is a gated Slack workspace for people who meet specific membership criteria. There is no treasury, no take-rate, no commissions, and no token sale. From its inception, Superteam chose to be a collective of sovereigns rather than a sovereign collective. Any revenue generated goes to the individual members or teams that self-organize and win a bounty, secure a grant, or raise venture funding for their ideas.

This structure matters because it shapes the incentive dynamics. Members are not contributing to a shared pool controlled by a central entity. They are independent operators who benefit from the network effects of being connected to other high-quality builders in the Solana ecosystem. The community is the product, and members have exclusive access to it.

sections.heading: Superteam India Workshop Details
content: The August 28 workshop is organized by Superteam India and hosted by Atharv Velhal. The session is virtual, with the exact platform to be announced. Registration requires approval, meaning you need to be accepted into the event rather than simply signing up. This gated approach is consistent with Superteam's overall philosophy of curating its community carefully.

The workshop falls under the broader umbrella of events that help talented people learn, earn, and build on Solana around the world. For those unfamiliar, Solana is a high-performance blockchain known for its speed and low transaction costs, which has attracted a large developer community building everything from DeFi protocols to consumer apps. Being part of Superteam India gives you direct access to opportunities within that ecosystem.

sections.heading: Office Hours and Community Rhythm
content: One of the regular touchpoints for Superteam India members is the weekly Office Hours, held every Tuesday at 6 PM. These are dedicated spaces for members to discuss ongoing projects, share feedback, and help shape the direction of the community. The consistency of this cadence is important. It means there is always a predictable channel for engagement, rather than relying on sporadic events or announcements.

For anyone considering joining Superteam India, the Office Hours represent the kind of ongoing value that distinguishes a living community from a one-off event series. The ability to regularly connect with peers working on similar problems in the Solana ecosystem is a genuine advantage, particularly for builders who might otherwise feel isolated working on their projects.

sections.heading: Who Should Apply
content: This workshop is most relevant for developers, operators, and founders who are actively building or planning to build on Solana. If you are a developer exploring Solana for the first time, the approval-based registration process means you will need to demonstrate some level of engagement or intent. This is not a barrier for the sake of exclusivity. It is a filtering mechanism that keeps the community focused and high-quality.

Superteam operates in many countries and regions, so being part of the India chapter connects you to both local and global networks. The combination of local workshops, global events like KUB Global, and the underlying Slack community creates multiple layers of engagement depending on your needs and availability.

sections.heading: The Broader Solana Skyline NYC Context
content: Solana Skyline NYC positions itself as the organizer of events for the Solana ecosystem in New York City. luma-host-evt-nHN886ANUexVx9b.summaryLead: Chainlink's August Community Pulse session goes live on August 28, 2026, featuring community advocates Amy Hang and Jordan Kull walking through the latest ecosystem updates, product milestones, and institutional developments in a concise 30-minute format.

sections.heading: What the Community Pulse Is
content: The Chainlink Community Pulse is a recurring live community session designed to keep participants informed about the latest developments across the Chainlink ecosystem. The August English edition runs for just 30 minutes, from 6:00 to 6:30 PM UTC, making it one of the more digestible community events in the Web3 space. It is streamed on YouTube, which lowers the barrier to entry significantly compared to platform-specific events that require separate accounts or downloads.

Chainlink positions this as more than a product update. The session aims to explain why specific developments matter for builders, users, institutions, and the wider blockchain industry. That context-setting is valuable because it connects technical changes to practical implications, helping attendees understand not just what happened but why it matters for their work.

sections.heading: August Topics and Updates
content: This month's session covers several significant areas. Chainlink's growing adoption is a central theme, along with the LINK:NYC event and CFTC engagement, which signals the project's continued push into institutional and regulatory conversations. Participation in the Technology Leaders Summit is also highlighted, reflecting Chainlink's ambition to be recognized as critical infrastructure rather than just a crypto-native tool.

On the technical side, the session will address CCIP migration, which refers to the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol that enables communication between different blockchains. Product updates and the Chainlink Privacy Bootcamp are also on the agenda. These topics collectively paint a picture of an ecosystem that is expanding both technically and institutionally, with privacy and interoperability as key focus areas.

sections.heading: Who Is Speaking
content: The session features Amy Hang and Jordan Kull, both serving as Chainlink Community Advocates. Community advocates play a specific role in the Chainlink ecosystem. They bridge the gap between the core team and the broader community, translating technical developments into accessible language and providing feedback channels for community concerns.

The event is also associated with Javier Salomón and Bharath Silagani, though the primary speakers for this edition are Amy and Jordan. Having community advocates lead the session rather than engineers or executives keeps the tone approachable and focused on what matters to users and developers rather than internal product roadmaps.

sections.heading: Chainlink's Broader Role
content: Chainlink describes itself as the industry-standard oracle platform, and the supporting evidence is substantial. The platform powers the majority of decentralized finance and has enabled tens of trillions in transaction value since its inception. Major financial institutions including Swift, Euroclear, Mastercard, Fidelity International, UBS, and ANZ have adopted Chainlink's standards and infrastructure. On the protocol side, Aave, GMX, Lido, and many others rely on Chainlink for data feeds and interoperability.

The project operates on a fee model where offchain and onchain revenue from enterprise adoption is converted to LINK tokens and stored in the Strategic Chainlink Reserve. This economic structure ties the token directly to real-world usage, which is a model that many other projects aspire to but few have achieved at this scale. Understanding this context helps explain why Chainlink's community updates carry real weight beyond just the immediate product announcements and ecosystem milestones being discussed.

mu-315286686.summaryLead: A free online session from Microsoft Reactor Redmond walks you through connecting the Real-Time Intelligence MCP server to an AI agent, letting you query streaming data from Fabric's Eventhouse using plain Spanish—no KQL required.

sections.heading: What This Session Covers
content: Real-time data is useful, but only if you can actually ask it questions without writing complex queries. That is the problem this session tackles head-on. Hosted by Microsoft Reactor Redmond on August 28, 2026, the workshop is part of an ongoing Spanish-language series exploring Microsoft Fabric's newest capabilities.

The focus is the Real-Time Intelligence (RTI) MCP server and how it plugs into an AI agent so you can interact with Eventhouse and Azure Data Explorer using natural language. The session runs entirely online, so you can attend from anywhere with a browser. Registration is free through Meetup, and the Microsoft Reactor Redmond page has the link you need to sign up.

What makes this session different from a typical Fabric overview is the hands-on focus. You are not watching slides about MCP in the abstract—you are building a working pipeline that connects a real-time data source to a natural language interface. That practical orientation is consistent across the Microsoft Reactor series.

sections.heading: Connecting MCP to an AI Agent
content: The core demo walks you through hooking up the RTI MCP server to an AI agent that can dynamically discover schemas and metadata from KQL databases. From a prompt written in Spanish, the agent generates optimized queries, runs them against live streaming data, and returns insights—all without you writing a single line of KQL.

Two server modes are covered: the local open-source read-only server for development and testing, and the remote hosted server that requires no installation at all. By the end you will have built a complete agentic query pipeline over real-time data, which is a pattern you can replicate in production once you are back at your desk.

The agent's ability to discover schemas dynamically is worth paying attention to. Rather than hardcoding table names and column mappings, the MCP server lets the agent figure out what data is available and how it is structured. That makes the pipeline more resilient to schema changes, which matters in streaming environments where data evolves fast.

sections.heading: Prerequisites and What to Prepare
content: Before the session starts, make sure you have access to an Eventhouse in your Fabric workspace with at least one table containing data. That is the only hard prerequisite listed by the organizers. A working familiarity with Fabric will help, but the session is designed to be approachable even if you are newer to the platform.

If you do not already have a Fabric workspace set up, the Microsoft Learn AI Hub—listed as a sponsor of this event—is a good place to start. The Copilot Hub is another resource worth bookmarking if you want to explore agent-based workflows after the session.

The event is free and hosted through Meetup, so registering on the Microsoft Reactor Redmond page gives you the join link. Given the interactive format, plan to attend live rather than relying on a recording.

sections.heading: Who Should Attend
content: Data engineers and analysts who work with streaming pipelines and want to reduce the barrier between asking a question and getting an answer will get the most out of this session. Developers building agentic AI workflows on top of Fabric will also find the multi-server approach useful as a reference architecture.

The Spanish-language delivery is worth noting: if you are more comfortable in Spanish, this is one of the few hands-on Fabric workshops that runs entirely in that language. It lowers the bar for Latin American and Spanish audiences who want practical Fabric training without the language friction.

If you have already attended earlier sessions in this series, this one builds on the concepts introduced previously and takes them into real-time territory specifically. The progression from batch-oriented Fabric work to streaming agentic queries is a natural next step.
